rules.title: Method instantiation requires a struct receiver
rules.statement: Demand-driven method instantiation applies only when the concrete receiver type is a (possibly zoned) struct; receivers of any other type kind produce no method instances.

rules.title: Overload matching by user name plus signature suffix
rules.statement: A method reference name M matches a struct method whose stored short-name S satisfies S == M or S == M ++ "__g__" ++ sig; every match is instantiated as a distinct overload, each keeping its own signature.

rules.title: Method-level type-params are not bound by struct instantiation
rules.statement: A method carrying type-params beyond the struct's own (e.g. `fn map<U>`) is NOT instantiated by the struct-driven monomorphization path; its method-level type-params can only be bound by an actual call site supplying them (turbofish/inference).

rules.title: Struct type-args bind struct type-params positionally with variadic tail
rules.statement: Concrete struct type-arguments bind to the struct's type-parameters left-to-right by position; a variadic type-parameter absorbs all remaining trailing type-arguments as one pack.

rules.title: Structured impl self-type gates method applicability by unification
rules.statement: When a method's impl has a structured target pattern (e.g. `impl<T> Pin<&T>`), the pattern's args are unified against the concrete struct's args: failure to unify means the method does not apply to this instantiation and is skipped; success merges the impl-level bindings (T) into the substitution alongside the struct-level bindings.

rules.title: Non-concrete or projection args defer applicability decision
rules.statement: When unifying an impl target pattern, a concrete struct arg that is null, contains a type-variable, or whose pattern position is an associated-type projection is not structurally decidable and is skipped (deferred to a later fully-concrete pass) rather than treated as a mismatch.

rules.title: Method instances dedup per concrete type and overload
rules.statement: At most one instance is produced per (concrete struct type, user-facing method name, overload short-name); overloads sharing one user-facing name collapse to a single slot per signature, matching eager-clone semantics.

rules.title: Concrete impl specialization preempts blanket method clone
rules.statement: If a non-generic `impl Foo<Concrete>` already provides a free function under the target method's mangled name, the blanket/generic method body is not cloned for that instantiation; the concrete specialization is used instead.
